description: An operator section passes the function that applies its operator to each item
A section reads the rest of its argument with the usual precedence, as if the item stood before the operator
Nullish and logical sections fill missing values and empty names with defaults
A standing section follows later writes of the names its operand reads and of its receiver
code:
limit = 20
readings = [12, 31, 7]
over = readings.filter(> limit)
limit = 10
readings.push(45)
over

description: Arithmetic sections give keys: * -1 sorts in descending order and % 10 picks by the last digit
Partition with a comparison section splits the items it keeps from the items it drops
A section is an ordinary function argument of user functions and constructors
A class-level rule's section reads each instance's own properties
code:
class Sensor(readings, limit):
    this.readings = readings
    this.limit = limit
$Sensor.alarms = $Sensor.readings.count(> $Sensor.limit)
north = Sensor([12, 31, 7], 20)
north.limit = 10
north.alarms

description: A section that fails for a new item rolls back the update that brought the item
code:
counts = [3, 5]
filled = counts.map(?? spare())
failure = ""
try:

catch error:
    failure = error
[failure, counts.length, filled]

description: Sections nest: the rest of a section may call a function with a section of its own
A section explains as function(), as an anonymous lambda does
Power and strict-equality sections compare and raise each item
